newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil's Sercomtel in B Band bid, plans offering.
newsitem.headline: Brazil's Sercomtel in B Band bid, plans offering.

text.p: Brazil's tiny Sercomtel SA municipal telecom plans to publicly issue securities and battle with the world's giants in the frenzied bidding for local cellular telephone concessions, a company official said.
"We have joined in a consortium with two Korean companies to bid on the B Band," Rubens Pavan, Sercomtel's finance and market relations chief, told Reuters in an interview.
He also said the company intends to begin listing shares on the Sao Paulo Stock Exchange by issuing $35 million in debentures convertible to preferred shares sometime in 1997's first half.

Servico de Comunicacoes Telefonicas de Londrina (Sercomtel), wholly owned by the southern city of Londrina, is Brazil's only municipally owned telecom and one of just three non-federal Brazilian operators. The others are state-owned CTBC and CRT.
With a net worth of $305 million, the firm is miniscule compared with Brazil's federal telecom Telebras or the foreign giants expected to join in the B Band bidding.

But the company has teamed with Samsung Corp and Korea Telecom to bid on the B Band concessions and the group is negotiating with a fourth firm to become the second local partner, Pavan said. "The fourth partner would fulfill the national contingent requirement for consortia," he said.
Sercomtel also plans to offer debentures convertible to shares to gain another source of cash and give the firm a higher profile, Pavan said.
He denied the move was linked to the firm's B Band plans. "We plan to launch debentures so that we have paper, stocks trading on the bolsa," he said.

The firm, which operates 120,000 fixed lines and 25,000 cellular terminals, expects to post gross sales this year of at least $120 million and net 1996 profit of up to $15 million, he said. Last year, Sercomtel posted a net profit of $5.2 million.
Investments by the company also are up this year, expected to reach $40 million versus $14 million in 1995.
"Our company is not very big but it is very efficient, has a great capacity to grow and has zero debt," he said.
